findings.title: Core lenses are not enforced; an approval can skip conformance and correctness
findings.fix: At an implementation gate, put `conformance` and `correctness` (and every planned, non-dropped lens) into `led["expect"]` inside `collect`/`plan`, not from the caller's flags. `compose` should return `rerun` when the conformance output has never been joined.

sources.situation: The expected lenses are only what the caller passes as `--expect`. At this gate `collect` never adds `conformance` and `correctness` to `expect`, and `compose` only reports `missing` for lenses already in `led["expect"]`. An agent runs `nio jury collect ... --expect adversary` and collects only the adversary output, or a conformance run dies and its file is never written. `compose` sees no missing lens. `join`, the only code that raises "AC has no passing evidence", runs only when a valid `implementation-E-n-conformance` file arrives. So no AC is ever checked against the results, and `nio jury check --record` can say `approved`. FR-14 says the two lenses always run, and FR-38 says a planned lens with no valid output never gives `approved`. Nothing in the CLI holds either.

findings.reason: `jury.collect` sets `led["expect"]` only from the `--expect` flags (jury.py:555). `compose` flags a missing lens only if it is in `expect` (jury.py:922). Nothing adds conformance or correctness at an implementation gate, so a round with only adversary output can compose to approved. `join` runs only when a valid conformance file arrives (jury.py:597-602).

findings.title: `--pick` is accepted when the plan is not over the cap, so one command silently drops risk lenses and the record blames the human
findings.fix: Accept `--pick` only when the plan is over the cap, and refuse otherwise. Keep a second pick from dropping a lens that already has collected output. Add `plan *--pick*` to the ASK patterns, or require a human flag, so the drop is the human's.

sources.situation: The branch tests only `pick is not None`. It does not test `over`. On an epic with 4 lenses and a cap of 6, an agent runs `nio jury plan s implementation-E-1 --pick conformance,correctness`. `security` (flag `auth`) and `adversary` (flag `external-input`) are written to `led["dropped"]`, and `collect` then refuses their outputs. `jury plan` is in `hooks.ALLOW`, and the ASK list has no `--pick` entry, so nothing prompts the human. The verdict then prints "Dropped lenses (the human's pick)", which credits the human with a choice they never made. A second `--pick` after round 1 can also drop a lens that has already blocked.

findings.reason: `plan` runs the `pick is not None` branch without checking `over` (jury.py:303-312). It writes `dropped` for the unpicked lenses, and `collect` then refuses those lenses. `hooks.ALLOW` holds "jury plan" and ASK (hooks.py:64) has no `--pick` pattern, so nothing asks the human.

findings.title: An `auto` journey whose steps don't parse is recorded as passed without running anything
quotes: ok = all(r["result"] == "passed" and matched(e, r["output"]) for r, (_, e) in zip(rs, ss))
findings.fix: A scenario marked `auto` that yields zero steps, or fewer steps than its numbered list, gets `result: "failed"` with an output saying so. Reject an empty `contains:` expectation. Print a line for each skipped or unparsed scenario.

sources.situation: `journeys()` keeps a scenario that has "; auto)" in its heading and finds its steps with a strict regex (a backticked command, `Expected:`, and a fenced block). A scenario with a slightly different layout, such as a missing fence or `Expected` written inline, parses to `[]`. In `collect`, `rs = []`, so `all(...)` over an empty list is `True`, and the journey is written as `"result": "passed"` with an empty command and empty output. No step ran. A multi-step scenario where one step is malformed is also quietly cut down to the steps that parse. An empty `contains:` line is also an automatic match, since `"" in output` is true. The lens sees a green journey, and no error or warning is printed.

findings.reason: `journeys()` returns `[]` steps when the regex doesn't match (evidence.py:117). In `collect`, `rs=[]` makes `all(...)` true, so the journey is written as "passed" (evidence.py:352-353). `matched` accepts an empty `contains:` because `"" in output` is true (evidence.py:125).

findings.title: With a test runner the CLI can't address, every scripted attack becomes "not configured" and every test "unknown", and both count as evidence
quotes: attack_cmds = [one_test(t.get("suite"), f, n) for f, n in mis]
findings.fix: Print `attacks: not configured` as `collect` does for lint and typecheck. Record each attack that could not run as a major finding, or at least a hint that every pack carries. In `join`, accept `unknown` only when the matched test is a def line the suite is known to reach, and never for `line == 0`.

sources.situation: `one_test` only knows `unittest` and `pytest`; for anything else it returns `None`, and `one()` turns an empty command into `"result": "not configured"`. This run shows the effect. The suite is a shell loop over `uv run python tests/test_*.py`. All four misuse attacks in `results.attacks` read `"result": "not configured"`, so the spec's misuse lines (FR-12) were never run, and the CLI printed nothing about it. `collect` prints "not configured" only for lint and typecheck. Every entry in `tests` is `"unknown"`, and `join` counts `unknown` the same as `passed`. Any test file the suite command doesn't reach, or a named test that is not in the file at all (the result shows one with `"line": 0` and `"unknown"`), therefore still counts as an AC's passing evidence while the suite exits 0. The attack results never become findings either way.

findings.reason: `one_test` returns None for any runner other than unittest or pytest (evidence.py:102-108). `one()` turns an empty command into "not configured" (evidence.py:31-32), and `collect` prints "not configured" only for lint and typecheck (evidence.py:363-364). A runner with no summary reader gives "unknown" when the suite passes (evidence.py:339), and `join` counts "unknown" as passing (evidence.py:390).

findings.title: `results.json` is never tied to the gate's epic or to the commit being judged
findings.fix: Store the slug, epic and head commit in `results.json`. In `collect`, `pack`, `join` and `requested`, fail with a ValueError if they differ from the gate's epic and `commits_of(...)[0]`, telling the caller to run `nio jury evidence` again.

sources.situation: `collect`, `pack` and `join` take the results from whatever `--run` names. They never compare `results["commit"]` with `commits_of(...)[0]`, and the file holds no slug or epic. Two cases follow. A fix task lands after a `rejected` round and the agent re-collects without re-running `nio jury evidence`. The old file still says the AC's test passed at the old commit, so `join` finds passing evidence for code that has since changed. Or the agent passes the run id of another epic's evidence. That file has other tests and another commit, and it is joined against this epic's ACs. In both cases FR-6 (evidence is only what was observed on this code) is broken, and no error is raised. The only guard is the text "run `nio jury evidence`" in a `rerun` reason, and that reason appears only when a fix verdict is waiting.

findings.reason: `collect`, `pack` and `join` take their results from `load(root, run)` and never compare `results["commit"]` with `commits_of(...)[0]`. The results file holds no slug or epic (evidence.py:355). In `jury.collect`, `join` runs on whatever file `--run` names (jury.py:600-601).

findings.title: Tampering dispose rule in CT-20 doesn't match the code's fix-task exception
quotes: - Fails: `dispose` of a `tampering` finding by anything but `--by human` → ValueError
findings.fix: Amend the CT-20 Fails line to say the refusal applies to every disposition except `fix-task` (accepting as risk, overruling and the other human-only dispositions stay with `--by human`), and keep the code. Or, if the literal line is right, change the code and the append_fix path. Human to rule which side is wrong (right: code is my view).

sources.situation: CT-20 says any dispose of a tampering finding that isn't `--by human` raises. The code is `if f.get("tampering") and by != "human" and disposition != "fix-task":`, so an agent can dispose of a tampering finding as `fix-task` (append_fix does this through jury.dispose(..., "fix-task", "agent", ...)). The code is the only way the FR-26 fix-task route works for a tampering finding, so the spec line is likely the stale one. As written, a reviewer following CT-20 would expect the agent's fix-task dispose to fail.

findings.reason: CT-20 (contracts.md:239) says a dispose of a tampering finding by anything but `--by human` fails. The code adds `and disposition != "fix-task"` (jury.py:841), so the two disagree. The code is what `append_fix` needs.

findings.title: The consistency lens's decision check has no decisions in its pack
quotes: - Read the epic's diff against the decisions in the pack: does the code contradict an `approved` or `current` decision, without a change request against it?
findings.fix: Add the related decisions and lessons with their standing to the implementation-gate pack (CT-9, for the consistency lens), or change the card to name the memory records the lens must read and how to find them.

sources.situation: The card's At implementation section tells consistency to check the epic's diff against approved or current decisions in its pack. CT-9's Accepts says the pack holds "the diff, the results, the hints, and spec and contract items", and evidence.pack builds sections for Diff, Items the diff touches, Results and Hints only. The lens gets no decision text and no standing (approved, current or superseded) for the decisions it should check, so the first bullet can't be run from the pack. Its repeat-a-rejected-approach bullet has the same gap. Concretely, the lens would have to search .nio/memory by itself, with no way to know which decisions the pack meant.

findings.reason: consistency.md:37 tells the lens to check the diff against the decisions in the pack. `evidence.pack` builds only Diff, Items the diff touches, Results and Hints (evidence.py:499-510). It has no memory or decision section, and evidence.py has no memory code at all.
findings.where: src/nio/evidence.py pack (the consistency lens's pack at implementation)

findings.title: results.json holds a `suite` key the CT-7 Shape doesn't list
findings.fix: Add `suite` to the CT-7 Shape with a one-line meaning (the suite's exit code and output, which the per-test results can't carry), or drop the key and print the suite's result under `checks`.

sources.situation: CT-7 gives the results.json Shape as the keys commit, tests, checks, attacks, journeys, hints, requests and evidence. collect writes `"tests": tests, "suite": suite, "checks": ...`, and the pack's Results section prints the `suite` object (command, result, output, cut). Packs and collect read it, so a reader of the spec would not know the key exists. Harmless, but the spec's Shape and the file disagree.

findings.where: src/nio/evidence.py collect (the results dict written by save)

findings.title: A conformance fix-check output with no `## Matches` section re-blocks every AC
quotes: evidence.join(root, slug, epic, matches[1].splitlines() if matches else [], results)
findings.fix: Run `join` only in a first-review round, or when the output has a `## Matches` section. In a fix-check round, keep the earlier evidence and let the CLI re-judge only its own `fix-task` entries. Alternatively, have the fix-check pack tell the conformance juror to repeat its Matches section.

sources.situation: `collect` calls `join` on every valid conformance output, in re-review and final fix-check rounds too. A fix-check pack asks for per-finding verdicts (`- J-n: fixed | not fixed`). The conformance card's Re-review text does not ask for matches, so a juror can reasonably omit `## Matches`. With `matches=[]`, `join` gives every AC the result "no match" and records a new blocker "AC-n has no passing evidence" for each AC that was not already flagged. It also overwrites `results["evidence"]` with no-match entries. An epic that was correct after its fix tasks is rejected again, or sent to the human, by findings that were never real. The only test of the no-Matches case (test_no_matches_section_leaves_each_ac_with_a_finding_and_the_epic_unapproved) runs a first-round collect. The re-review tests' `impl_out` helper always writes `E1_MATCHES`, which hides this path.

findings.reason: `jury.collect` calls `join` for every new valid conformance file, passing `[]` when there is no `## Matches` section (jury.py:597-602). `join` then gives every AC "no match" and a blocker (evidence.py:381-393). The re-review pack asks only for `- J-n: fixed | not fixed` verdicts (evidence.py:488), and the Re-review section of conformance.md:39-41 doesn't ask for Matches.
findings.where: src/nio/jury.py (collect, the call to evidence.join) and src/nio/evidence.py:join

findings.title: An AC proved by a misuse test is judged "didn't run" and gets a blocker
quotes: ponytail: a match counts only when its line is a test's own `def` line in the results.
findings.fix: Also put the misuse tests into `results["tests"]` with file, line and result, or let `join` accept a match against the attack entries. Record the file and line on each attack entry so the match can be checked.

sources.situation: `collect` puts only the non-misuse tests of tests.md (the `rest` list) into `results["tests"]`. Misuse tests go into `attacks`, as `{command, result, output, cut}` with no file or line. `join` looks up the conformance lens's `file:line` in `results["tests"]` only. If the lens correctly matches an AC to its misuse or attack test, the lookup finds nothing and the result is "didn't run". If that is the AC's only test, the AC gets a blocker even though the attack ran and passed. Abuse-case ACs (for example the AC-3 style refusals) are the likeliest to be proved this way. The false blocker comes from the CLI, not a juror, so the refuter never sees it, and only a human can dispose of it.

findings.reason: Misuse tests go only into `attacks`, which carry no file or line (evidence.py:343-346). Only `rest` tests enter `results["tests"]` (evidence.py:336-342). `join` looks a match up in `results["tests"]` only (evidence.py:378, 382-383). An AC proved only by a misuse test therefore gets "didn't run" and a blocker.

findings.title: A fix task's `Files:` is built from the juror's free-text `where`, which can create a phantom the next evidence run reports
quotes: where = ", ".join("`" + re.sub(r":\d+(-\d+)?$", "", f) + "`" for f in files(finding["where"]))
findings.fix: In `append_fix`, keep only `where` pieces that exist as tracked files (after stripping `:line`). If none do, fall back to the files named in the finding's quote or cites, or to the epic's changed files, as `check_finding` does with `named_files`.

sources.situation: The card allows `where: <file or area>`. `files()` splits on commas and wraps each piece in backticks. A `where` such as "the evidence module, src/nio/jury.py" or "src/a.py lines 12-20" becomes `Files:` entries that are not paths. `phantoms` runs on every task of the epic, fix tasks included, so on the next `nio jury evidence` each such entry is reported as a new major CLI finding, "T-n: <area> doesn't exist". The worker also cannot make that task's file list match any real path, so a task that finished honestly keeps the epic rejected. The join finding with `where: ac` has the same problem when no files are known.

findings.reason: `append_fix` builds `Files:` from `files(finding["where"])`, which splits on commas and backticks each piece with no check that it is a path (tasks.py:381). The conformance card allows `where: <file or area>` (conformance.md:29). `phantoms` reports any task file not found at head as a major finding (evidence.py:170-172), and it runs over every task of the epic, fix tasks included.
